name: centinel-dev-lifecycle
description: Adaptive development lifecycle for Centinel: supports both Static and Dynamic testing modules. Ingest artifacts, select module, human approval, iterative development with requirement-to-code validation, and final documentation.

data.description: Collect and analyze all project artifacts: PRD, docs, existing code, requirements, and design specs.
data.agentDefinition: Investigation agent that scans the repository for all relevant project artifacts.
data.prompt: Scan the entire repository and collect all project artifacts. Read the PRD (Centinel_PRD_Revised.md), PROJECT_PLAN.md, any docs/, existing source code (centinel/, sidecar/), configuration files, and design documents. Produce a structured summary of: (1) all functional requirements for BOTH static and dynamic modules, (2) non-functional requirements, (3) system architecture decisions, (4) existing code coverage and what's already built, (5) gaps between requirements and current implementation. Pay special attention to: Static module scope (artifact review, MiMo prompts, findings schema) and Dynamic module scope (Playwright-Gemini loop, action executor, evidence capture). Output a comprehensive artifact inventory.

data.questionText: Which module are you working on? This shapes the plan, prompts, and review criteria.

options.label: Centinel Static
options.description: Artifact review, MiMo prompt design, inconsistency detection, requirement-to-code traceability, static findings and reports

options.label: Centinel Dynamic
options.description: Playwright-Gemini loop, autonomous UI testing, action executor, evidence capture, dynamic bug reports

options.label: Shared Platform
options.description: Desktop shell, navigation, project management, SQLite schema, UI components, unified reporting

data.description: Create a module-specific implementation plan based on ingested artifacts and selected module.
data.agentDefinition: Architecture and planning agent that designs implementation plans tailored to the selected Centinel module.
data.prompt:
Based on the artifact inventory and the user's selected module, create a feature-level implementation plan.

IMPORTANT: Present the plan at the FEATURE level with ABSTRACT implementation descriptions. Do NOT list specific files or code. For each feature, describe:
- WHAT the feature does (user-facing capability)
- HOW it works abstractly (architecture, data flow, key concepts)
- Dependencies on other features

If STATIC module, structure as these features:
1. Artifact Management — upload, store, organize artifacts per project
2. Static Review Engine — AI-powered analysis with 4 review types (requirement quality, code inspection, cross-artifact consistency, requirement-to-code traceability)
3. Structured Findings — standardized findings with severity, accept/dismiss workflow
4. Report Generation — export review results as readable documents
5. Project & Session Management — projects, review history, session tracking
6. Findings UI — browse, filter, view details, take action on findings

If DYNAMIC module, structure as these features:
1. Browser Session Management — launch, target URL, mission goals
2. Action Loop Engine — capture state → AI decision → execute action → record evidence
3. Supported Actions — click, type, navigate, scroll, assert, wait, finish
4. Evidence Capture — screenshots per step, action traces, console logs
5. Safety Limits — step count cap, timeout, domain restriction
6. Dynamic Bug Report Generation — structured reports from session evidence
7. Session UI — run sessions, view progress, browse evidence

If SHARED PLATFORM, structure as these features:
1. Data Model & Storage — SQLite schema, project/artifact/session/finding entities
2. Project Management — create, open, delete projects
3. Navigation & Layout — sidebar, routing, shared shell
4. Settings — API key configuration
5. Unified Findings — cross-module findings list
6. Report Export — combined static+dynamic reports

For each feature, include: what it does, how it works abstractly, and its dependency order. Output a plan ready for human review.

data.questionText: Review the implementation plan. How would you like to proceed?

options.label: Request Changes
options.description: Need modifications to the plan before proceeding

options.label: Ask Questions
options.description: Need clarification on specific parts of the plan

data.label: Q&A Session
data.prompt: The user has questions about the plan. Engage in a Q&A session to clarify any ambiguities, explain technical decisions, and address concerns. Reference the PRD and PROJECT_PLAN.md when answering. After answering, summarize what was clarified and re-present the plan for approval.

data.description: Implement code according to the approved plan for the selected module.
data.agentDefinition: Code generation agent that implements software according to the approved plan. Adapts behavior based on whether the selected module is Static, Dynamic, or Shared.
data.prompt:
Implement the code according to the approved plan for the selected module.

For STATIC module tasks: Implement artifact upload/parsing, design MiMo prompt templates for each review type (requirement review, code review, cross-artifact consistency, requirement-to-code traceability), build the static review runner that sends prompts to MiMo and parses structured JSON responses, implement finding storage and schema validation, build the findings UI with accept/dismiss workflow, and create report export.

For DYNAMIC module tasks: Implement the Playwright browser session runner, build the Gemini action decision loop (screenshot → DOM snapshot → Gemini prompt → action → execute → evidence), implement the action executor for all supported actions, build evidence capture (screenshots per step, action trace, console logs), implement safety limits (max steps, timeout, domain restriction), and create dynamic bug report generation.

For SHARED PLATFORM tasks: Set up SQLite schema with all tables, implement Tauri commands or sidecar endpoints for CRUD operations, build React routing and navigation, create project management UI, settings page, and shared layout.

For each task: (1) Create or modify specified files, (2) Write clean well-structured code, (3) Add comments and documentation, (4) Handle error cases, (5) Follow dependency order. Provide a summary of all files created/modified.

data.description: Review implemented code against module-specific requirements. Run tests, validate behavior.
data.agentDefinition: QA agent that reviews code against requirements. Uses module-specific review criteria for Static, Dynamic, or Shared modules.
data.prompt:
Perform a comprehensive review and test of the implemented code for the selected module.

For STATIC module review criteria: (1) Does artifact upload work for .txt, .md, .js, .ts, .py files? (2) Do MiMo prompts return structured JSON with required fields (title, severity, category, artifactReference, description, evidence, recommendation, confidence)? (3) Are findings stored and retrievable? (4) Does accept/dismiss workflow work? (5) Is report export functional?

For DYNAMIC module review criteria: (1) Does Playwright launch and capture screenshots? (2) Does the action loop correctly cycle through capture → decide → execute → evidence? (3) Are all supported actions implemented (click, type, press_key, scroll, wait, navigate, assert_visible, finish_success, finish_failure)? (4) Do safety limits enforce step count and timeout? (5) Is evidence properly saved and linked? (6) Does the bug report include all required sections?

For SHARED PLATFORM review criteria: (1) Does SQLite schema match the data model in PROJECT_PLAN.md? (2) Do CRUD operations work for projects, artifacts, sessions, findings, evidence? (3) Is navigation working between all pages? (4) Are empty/loading/error states handled?

General review: Map each PRD requirement to implementing code, review code quality, run available tests, identify defects. Output: PASS/FAIL, requirement coverage, defects found, fix recommendations.

branches.label: All Requirements Met
branches.condition: Review passes: all module-specific requirements covered, no critical defects, code matches PRD specifications

branches.label: Issues Found
branches.condition: Review fails: missing requirements, defects found, or behavior doesn't match specs

data.description: Fix identified defects and implement missing requirements for the selected module.
data.agentDefinition: Bug fix and refinement agent that addresses issues found during review. Adapts to the selected module context.
data.prompt: Based on the review findings for the selected module: (1) Fix each identified defect with the specific file and line reference, (2) Implement any missing requirement coverage, (3) Correct any behavior that doesn't match the PRD specs, (4) After fixes, do a quick self-review to verify the changes address all issues. For Static fixes: ensure MiMo prompts produce valid JSON, findings schema is correct, report export works. For Dynamic fixes: ensure action loop terminates correctly, evidence is captured per step, safety limits are enforced, bug reports are complete. For Shared fixes: ensure SQLite operations are correct, navigation works, UI states are handled. Output a summary of all changes made and which issues were resolved.

data.description: Generate final documentation at /docs as future reference for the implemented module.
data.agentDefinition: Documentation agent producing comprehensive project docs tailored to the selected module.
data.prompt:
Generate documentation at /docs for the selected module. Create:

(1) docs/DEVELOPMENT_LOG.md — chronological record of all development actions, decisions, and iterations performed during this workflow run.

(2) docs/ARCHITECTURE.md — system architecture, module structure, design decisions. For Static: document the MiMo prompt pipeline, finding schema, review workflow types. For Dynamic: document the Playwright-Gemini action loop, evidence capture pipeline, safety limits.

(3) docs/REQUIREMENTS_TRACEABILITY.md — mapping of each PRD requirement to its implementing code with status (implemented/partial/not implemented).

(4) docs/IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md — file-by-file summary, key functions and their purposes, API endpoints or Tauri commands added.

(5) docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md — remaining issues, technical debt, future improvements.

Make each document thorough enough as future reference for anyone joining the project.
